finding: For the SAME actual finite UD code D, if tail residues j,k differ by one of ±{3,5,8,11}, their head supports C_j and C_k are disjoint. Otherwise one head occurring in both columns would give two same-head one-b atoms whose tail difference matches a difference between actual zero-tail old heads A={0,3,8,11}; padded two-word parses would collide. All differences are taken modulo the actual n, and the argument uses genuine actual atoms and a^n-boundary padding.
integer_check: The eval kernel enumerated all 28 unordered old-column pairs and obtained exactly the six listed edges. It also checked each literal old head-support intersection for these six edges is empty. For n>=26 no extra wrap edge occurs among the eight residues: all positive differences are ≤14 and n−d cannot equal 3,5,8,11 unless n is smaller than the relevant threshold; near n=26, check the edge list directly before adopting it.
scope_caveat: The algebraic disjointness statement modulo n is universal. The displayed positive-difference edge list is exact whenever n>25 AND no wrap gap n−d lies in {3,5,8,11}; its exact least uniform threshold must be independently checked. This checkpoint makes no all-order claim from the graph alone.
blocker: The graph on these eight columns has no triangles, and each individual column capacity is about n/5; simple pairwise disjointness and cardinality cannot alone imply a stronger global lower bound. A new joint cross-shift or full path invariant is required. No claim that other column pairs are disjoint is made.
status: WRITTEN plus exact finite integer enumeration; not independently reviewed, formally verified, or novelty cleared. Original problem remains OPEN.
